PullRequest.Title: chat: Hide unavailable MCP Gallery source
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Hide MCP Gallery from the Browse customizations source picker when no MCP gallery manifest is configured or available.

The platform marketplace services now derive MCP Gallery source availability from `IMcpGalleryManifestService` and notify consumers when that availability changes, allowing the picker to update dynamically after configuration changes.

## Validation

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/customizationMarketplace/common/mcpGalleryMarketplaceProvider.ts src/vs/platform/customizationMarketplace/electron-browser/customizationMarketplaceService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/customizationMarketplaceWorkbenchService.ts src/vs/platform/customizationMarketplace/test/common/mcpGalleryMarketplaceProvider.test.ts src/vs/platform/customizationMarketplace/test/electron-browser/customizationMarketplaceService.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — blocked before compilation because `package.json` declares Copilot runtime `1.0.99-2`, while the installed `@github/copilot-sdk` bundles `1.0.98-2`.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — blocked by existing Agent Host/Copilot SDK type mismatches; no errors were reported in the changed files.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The delayed web registration, initial status, network-awaiting initialization, immediate first catalog load, forced source-event reload, and per-provider query fan-out are all directly traced. Exact latency depends on registry and provider response times, but duplicate or partially duplicated boundary work is deterministic when the first catalog load starts before version negotiation completes.
Findings.PerformanceResource: network requests to every enabled non-MCP customization marketplace provider, plus the MCP manifest version probe
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On VS Code Web, one opening of Browse Customizations while a custom MCP gallery without an explicit version initializes causes the first catalog request to fan out across all enabled non-MCP providers; when the manifest probe completes, the source event cancels that request and fans out across those providers again. The duplicate count grows with configured plugin/provider marketplaces and other enabled feeds.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: extra network I/O and a restarted loading critical path, increasing time to stable Browse results
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, MCP was present in `sources` immediately. The first combined query started all providers once; the MCP provider awaited the same coalesced manifest initialization while the other providers ran in parallel, so manifest discovery did not require a second whole-catalog query.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The platform source list now temporarily omits MCP during asynchronous manifest initialization, publishes non-MCP results from an initial all-sources query, then announces a source change that invalidates and reloads the whole catalog after initialization.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added getter at line 36 now excludes MCP whenever the delayed web manifest service is still in its initial `Unavailable` state, while the added constructor call at line 45 starts asynchronous initialization. Completion then flows through the newly exposed source-change event and forces the consumer to reload.
Findings.Title: Avoid the two-phase catalog load while manifest availability initializes
Findings.Impact: In web sessions using a custom version-negotiated MCP registry, opening Browse Customizations can issue duplicate plugin/feed/connector catalog requests and reset the loading UI after the potentially slow registry probe. More configured marketplaces produce more duplicated requests.
Findings.Evidence: `IMcpGalleryManifestService` is delayed in `workbench.web.main.ts`; `WorkbenchMcpGalleryManifestService` initializes `currentStatus` to `Unavailable`, and a custom URL with no version awaits serial `checkVersion` network requests before `update()` emits the status event. The changed constructor starts that work, while this changed getter omits MCP until it completes. `AiCustomizationDiscoveryPage.setVisible()` immediately calls `loadCatalog(false)`; its source-change listener calls `scheduleMarketplaceRefresh(true)`, whose `handleAvailabilityChanged(true)` cancels the request, clears the browse cache, and calls `loadCatalog(false)` again. `CustomizationMarketplaceService.query()` invokes every selected provider concurrently, so all non-MCP feeds already started by the first query are invoked again.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not expose the initialization placeholder as a real unavailable source state. Preserve MCP in the source set while availability is unknown (for example with an explicit initializing/unknown state), letting its provider await the coalesced manifest promise in the first combined query; only publish a source change once initialization establishes that MCP is actually unavailable or later changes availability.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Browse Customizations in VS Code Web with a custom MCP gallery URL whose version must be negotiated
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The delayed platform marketplace service starts manifest initialization, but the initial `sources` read omits MCP. The visible discovery page immediately starts a combined query for the remaining sources. Progress is restarted only after the manifest version probe completes and the new source event forces a second combined query.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe the custom MCP registry for a supported version with `GET .../{version}/servers?limit=1`
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful GET, or up to two serial GETs when versions fail/are unsupported
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same probe was reached by the MCP provider in the first combined query; the PR moves initialization ahead of provider use but does not duplicate the probe because `initPromise` coalesces it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The status remains `Unavailable` until this completes, determining when the second catalog wave begins.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the first marketplace page from each enabled plugin/provider/GitHub/connector feed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before: once per enabled provider. After: non-MCP providers can be invoked in the initial wave and once again after MCP becomes available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: MCP was present in the initial source set; its provider awaited the coalesced manifest promise while all providers participated in one catalog wave.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The forced refresh cancels and discards the first wave, restarts loading, and requires the second wave before stable results are shown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of enabled/configured non-MCP marketplace providers. The effective duplicate cardinality is one additional first-page query per enabled non-MCP provider whose first request starts before manifest negotiation completes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Manifest versions are checked serially (up to two GETs). Each catalog wave fans out concurrently with `Promise.all` across selected providers; the second wave starts after cancellation of the first, but cancellation does not recover network work already issued.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: `initPromise` coalesces manifest initialization, so the version probe itself is not duplicated. The discovery browse cache starts cold and is explicitly cleared by the forced source refresh; warm manifest state avoids the two-wave behavior on later openings in the same service lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: delayed registration, transient unavailable status, immediate catalog loading, forced cache invalidation, and concurrent per-provider fan-out are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact duplicated bytes and delay depend on registry negotiation latency, provider count, cancellation responsiveness, and whether individual feeds complete before the status event.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: the transient initialization state introduced by the changed getter creates a second whole-catalog request wave.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Browse Customizations in desktop VS Code with the product MCP gallery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The desktop manifest service is eagerly instantiated and initializes before the delayed platform marketplace service is normally requested. The added constructor call observes/coalesces warm initialization; the first visible catalog query includes MCP and runs once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch first pages from enabled marketplace providers
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per selected provider on a cold first page
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider fan-out occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These calls determine first catalog results.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled marketplace provider count for the first page.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One concurrent `Promise.all` wave across selected providers; no added aggregate burst from the changed code once manifest status is warm.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The manifest service's initialization promise and current manifest are warm. The discovery cache is cold on first open but is populated from one request wave.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for normal desktop lifecycle based on eager singleton registration and delayed platform service registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: An unusually early consumer could observe initialization in progress, but normal desktop registration is eager and the product manifest construction itself requires no version-probe network request.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional regression: warm/coalesced manifest initialization leaves the established one-wave query behavior intact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change MCP gallery configuration while the customization UI is open
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The manifest service recomputes the active manifest, emits status/source changes, and visible consumers refresh source lists and marketplace content. Discovery refreshes are scheduled through a zero-delay coalescer; widget refreshes are mostly visibility/mode guarded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Negotiate a newly configured custom registry version
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero with an explicit version; otherwise one or up to two serial probe GETs
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manifest recomputation on this configuration change already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A source update based on the new manifest waits for negotiation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload visible combined marketplace results after source identity or availability changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced refresh in immediate transitions; slow version negotiation can separate configuration and status notifications, with work bounded to a user-driven configuration action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configuration-dependent refresh existed for service URL changes; the PR additionally propagates manifest status completion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Refresh is required before results reflect the new registry.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live consumers and enabled marketplace providers; configuration changes are user-driven rather than per-frame or per-item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Manifest version probes are serial; the unified catalog query fans out concurrently by provider. Discovery uses a `RunOnceScheduler` to coalesce same-turn configuration/source notifications.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Manifest initial initialization remains coalesced; configuration recomputation is not cached as the old initialization promise. Discovery deliberately clears its browse cache when source identity/availability changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for event propagation and refresh reachability; moderate for duplicated completed boundary work on a specific settings transition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether a slow custom-version transition starts an obsolete first request depends on timer/network ordering and provider cancellation, and the trigger is an infrequent explicit settings action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding beyond the reported two-phase initialization mechanism: the transition is user-driven, coalesced when immediate, and the completion refresh is needed to expose the authoritative manifest.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and traced web/desktop manifest lifecycle, source events, discovery/widget consumers, caches, provider fan-out, cancellation, and network boundaries. Submitted one medium-confidence-severity finding for duplicate whole-catalog network waves caused by treating delayed web manifest initialization as actual unavailability.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
